clue.text: Leakage points to the Head

parts.note: two compass points, East and South, give E and S
a cape is a headland, a head of land jutting into the sea

explanation.surface: A complaint that the leaks in the building all trace back to the headmaster.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to the' only joins the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: An escape of gas or water is a leak, the stuff getting out.

clue.text: Oriental jesters comprehend no financial skills

parts.note: E is short for East, and Oriental means eastern

indicators.note: to comprehend is to take in or include, so one piece holds the other inside it

parts.note: jesters are comics, comedians
taken as written

explanation.surface: Eastern clowns are said to have no head for money.
explanation.walkthrough: 'comprehend' puts NO inside COMICS, and E stands in front.
explanation.definitionFit: The study of money, trade and wealth is this discipline, so skills in finance fit it loosely.

clue.text: Eccentric circles of churchmen

indicators.note: eccentric means off-centre or odd, telling us to rearrange the letters of the next word

explanation.surface: Odd social circles made up of churchmen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Eccentric' rearranges CIRCLES; 'of' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Clergy, priests and ministers are churchmen.

clue.text: One needs to be in condition to get Poles' victuals

indicators.note: the word one needs to be in, placed inside, the word meaning condition

parts.note: a proviso is a condition attached to an agreement
I is the Roman numeral one
the two poles, North and South, give N and S

explanation.surface: Someone must be fit to collect rations meant for Polish people.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to be in' sets I inside PROVISO, giving PROVISIO, then NS follows; 'needs' and 'get' are links. 'Poles' looks like the people of Poland, but it means the Earth's poles.
explanation.definitionFit: Victuals are food supplies, the stores laid in for a journey.

clue.text: Many a figure abroad America?

parts.note: numero is the word for number in Italian and Spanish, a figure in a foreign tongue
US, the United States

explanation.surface: Asking whether a great many statistics come from overseas, from America perhaps.
explanation.walkthrough: The printed clue has a dash before 'America'; 'a' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Numerous things are a great many in number.

clue.text: Clara Peggotty's husband was not thus intestate

definitions.text: Clara Peggotty's husband was not thus

explanation.surface: A Dickens character's husband apparently died without leaving a will.
explanation.walkthrough: In Dickens's David Copperfield, Clara Peggotty's suitor Barkis famously sent the message 'Barkis is willin''. So he was not reluctant. Someone intestate is literally 'un-willed', dying with no will.
explanation.definitionFit: Barkis was eager to marry Clara, the opposite of reluctant; and a person who dies intestate has left no will.

clue.text: Pound for the scribe

explanation.surface: A pound handed over to pay the clerk.
explanation.walkthrough: Pound is the American poet, not money; the scribe is the Old Testament priest and scribe of the Book of that name.
explanation.definitionFit: The poet Pound's first name, and the name of the biblical scribe who brought the Law back to Jerusalem.

clue.text: Exterior is due to get repaired

indicators.note: something repaired is put back together differently, so these letters are reassembled

explanation.surface: The outside of the house needs mending soon.
explanation.walkthrough: 'get repaired' rearranges IS DUE TO.
explanation.definitionFit: The exterior of something is its outer side.

clue.text: Doomed city thus has Benedictine support

indicators.note: in a down answer the monk's title is placed underneath, holding up the word for thus

parts.note: so means thus, in this way
Dom is the title given to a Benedictine monk

explanation.surface: A city facing ruin is backed by the monks of a Benedictine house.
explanation.walkthrough: 'has' is a link; 'support' puts DOM below SO in the down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: The biblical city destroyed by fire and brimstone along with Gomorrah.

clue.text: Big South African mountain

parts.note: OS stands for outsize, a clothing label for large sizes
SA is the abbreviation for South Africa

explanation.surface: A huge peak in South Africa.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Big South African' looks like a description of the peak, but it gives the letters; the peak is in Greece, piled on Pelion by the giants in myth.
explanation.definitionFit: A mountain in Thessaly, Greece, famous from the myth of the giants piling Pelion on it.

clue.text: May possibly soon rue such a task

definitions.text: May possibly soon rue such a task

indicators.note: possibly says the letters could be arranged another way

explanation.surface: Someone taking on a heavy job may soon regret it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'possibly' rearranges SOON RUE; 'May' is a link, and the whole clue describes the kind of task one regrets.
explanation.definitionFit: A burdensome, heavy task is one you might quickly regret taking on.

clue.text: Fabric of defeat?

parts.note: a cloth whose name is also a word for beaten or bested, so a material made of defeat

explanation.surface: Asking what material a defeat is made of.
explanation.walkthrough: The wool cloth shares its spelling with the past tense of the verb meaning to get the better of someone.
explanation.definitionFit: A smooth wool yarn and cloth, and also a word for beaten or bested.

clue.text: Single, gin taken in by the mouth as a starter

indicators.note: taken in means swallowed or held inside, so the next pieces go within the word for by mouth

parts.note: orally means by the mouth, as with medicine
I, the Roman numeral one, single
taken as written

explanation.surface: One gin swallowed as a starter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'taken in' puts I and GIN inside ORALLY. 'gin taken in by the mouth' reads like drinking, but 'by the mouth' is the container.
explanation.definitionFit: Something done at first, at the beginning, was done at the outset, in its first form.

clue.text: Steady company

explanation.surface: A dependable business.
explanation.definitionFit: Firm means stable and unwavering; a firm is also a business partnership or company.

clue.text: Macbeth would make one of these double sure

definitions.text: Macbeth would make one of these double sure

parts.words: Macbeth would make one of these double sure
parts.note: Macbeth says he will make a promise or guarantee doubly certain, so the plural of that word is wanted

explanation.surface: A line from Macbeth about making something doubly certain.
explanation.walkthrough: In Shakespeare's Macbeth (Act 4), Macbeth says "I'll make assurance double sure" before resolving to kill Macduff.
explanation.definitionFit: Guarantees and pledges, the kind of certainty Macbeth wanted to double.

clue.text: Animate in one of Eton's distant features

parts.note: taken as written
Gray's Ode on a Distant Prospect of Eton College opens 'Ye distant spires, ye antique towers'

explanation.surface: Bringing life to one of Eton College's far-off landmarks.
explanation.walkthrough: Thomas Gray's poem about Eton College, the English boys' school, begins with its 'distant spires'.
explanation.definitionFit: To inspire someone is to fill them with life and enthusiasm, to stir them.

clue.text: It's unruly, but no one turns up

definitions.text: It's unruly, but no one turns up

parts.words: It's unruly, but no one turns up
parts.note: something unruly does not follow the rule; 'but' can mean 'except', and when none appears there is none of these

explanation.surface: Something is disorderly, yet nobody arrives.
explanation.walkthrough: Plays on 'the one that proves the rule', something outside the rule, and on the phrase 'without one'.
explanation.definitionFit: An instance that does not fit the rule, something left out or excluded.

clue.text: Portsmouth 12 six-footer comes round to examine

indicators.note: the creature goes round, enclosing, the single letter

parts.note: an insect has six legs, so it is a six-footer

indicators.note: 12 points to the answer at 12 across, meaning at the start, so take the first letter

explanation.surface: A six-foot man from Portsmouth walks round to look things over.
explanation.walkthrough: '12' cross-refers to 12 across, which means at the start, so it takes the opening P of Portsmouth; 'comes round' puts INSECT around it.
explanation.definitionFit: To inspect is to look closely at, to scrutinise.

clue.text: Handling by tamer, perhaps, in the Big Top

indicators.note: the rearranged letters go inside the circus marquee

parts.note: the big top is the circus tent

indicators.note: perhaps hints the word could be in another form, so its letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: How a lion tamer deals with his animals in the circus.
explanation.walkthrough: 'perhaps' rearranges TAMER to REATM, and 'in' puts that inside TENT; 'by' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: The way something is dealt with or managed, its handling.

clue.text: If I cast wildly about, in such devilish form …

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the rearranged letters go round the word for if
wildly says the letters are thrown about into a new order

parts.note: an is an old word for if, as in Shakespeare's 'an it please you'

explanation.surface: A fiend imagines what form he would take if he cast spells wildly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wildly' rearranges I CAST to SATIC, and 'about' puts that around AN. 'in such ... form' links the definition, and the clue leads on to 21 across.
explanation.definitionFit: Satanic means fiendish, of the Devil.

clue.text: Vexes the heartless City

parts.note: tries means vexes or strains, as in trying one's patience

indicators.note: heartless means losing the centre, so the middle letter of 'the' goes

explanation.surface: The heartless capital is a source of annoyance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heartless' drops the H from THE, leaving TE.
explanation.definitionFit: A port city in north-eastern Italy, on the Adriatic.

clue.text: … stick around — company's somewhat sweet

indicators.note: around says the word for stick goes round the next piece

parts.note: glue is an adhesive that makes things stick
CO is the abbreviation for company, with the 's adding S

explanation.surface: Continuing 19, a pleasant companion urges someone to stay put.
explanation.walkthrough: 'around' puts COS inside GLUE.
explanation.definitionFit: The simple sugar dextrose tastes sweet, though less so than cane sugar.

clue.text: Crude" violin, 'note, of chrysolite

indicators.note: crude means rough or unrefined, signalling the letters of the instrument be reworked

parts.note: E is a note of the musical scale

explanation.surface: A roughly made violin with a note on a gemstone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Crude' rearranges VIOLIN; then E follows. 'of' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Chrysolite is the green gem variety of this mineral, a magnesium iron silicate.

clue.text: Vessel in which Simon hunted a whale

definitions.text: Vessel in which Simon hunted a whale

parts.words: Vessel in which Simon hunted a whale
parts.note: the nursery rhyme Simple Simon goes fishing for a whale in his mother's bucket

explanation.surface: A ship from which someone named Simon went whaling.
explanation.walkthrough: In the nursery rhyme, 'Simple Simon went a-fishing for to catch a whale; all the water he had got was in his mother's pail'. 'Vessel' suggests a ship, but it is a bucket.
explanation.definitionFit: A bucket, the container where Simple Simon went fishing.

clue.text: Trojan capital

explanation.surface: A capital city of Troy.
explanation.definitionFit: The Trojan prince who carried off Helen, and the French capital city.

clue.text: But he's generally available for consultation

definitions.text: But he's generally available for consultation

parts.words: But he's generally available for consultation
parts.note: a doctor one consults who is the opposite of a general practitioner, so not general

explanation.surface: Someone usually free to give advice.
explanation.walkthrough: 'But' turns the sense: a consultant who is not a generalist, focusing on one field.
explanation.definitionFit: A consultant doctor who concentrates on one field rather than general practice.

clue.text: The fellow's up the wall!

explanation.surface: The man is going mad.
explanation.walkthrough: Cove is old British slang for a chap. A cove is also the concave moulding where a wall meets the ceiling, so it is up the wall. ''s' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Old slang for a chap or man, and the curved moulding at the top of a wall.

clue.text: Bottle for girl and boy.

parts.note: Vi is short for the girl's name Violet
Al is short for the boy's name Albert or Alan

explanation.surface: A small bottle meant for two youngsters.
explanation.definitionFit: A small glass bottle for medicine or scent.

clue.text: Composer's name for Lawrence in one

parts.note: T. E. Lawrence enlisted in the RAF under the assumed name John Hume Ross
taken as written
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: The composer's name, for Lawrence, rolled into one.
explanation.walkthrough: T. E. Lawrence (of Arabia) used the alias Ross when he joined the RAF. The definition 'Composer's' reads as 'Composer is' with the link.
explanation.definitionFit: The Italian operatic composer of The Barber of Seville.

clue.text: Wine producer includes a small quantity from a cow

indicators.note: includes means holds within, so the vine contains the next pieces

parts.note: a vine produces the grapes for wine
cc, a cubic centimetre, is a small measured quantity

explanation.surface: A winemaker adds a little milk from a cow.
explanation.walkthrough: 'includes' puts A and CC inside VINE. The word comes from Latin vacca, cow, as the first one was cowpox matter.
explanation.definitionFit: The first immunising matter was taken from cowpox, and its name comes from the Latin for cow.

clue.text: Crescendo of music without measure

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside, so the music goes round the measure

parts.note: swing is a style of jazz music
an ell is an old measure of length for cloth

explanation.surface: A rise in volume in music with no fixed beat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' here means outside, putting SWING round ELL; 'of' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A crescendo is a gradual rise in loudness, a surge.

clue.text: Going up a trail

parts.note: a scent is the trail an animal leaves for hounds to follow

explanation.surface: Climbing a path up a hill.
explanation.definitionFit: A climb, the act of rising.
